name: The Lowell
positioning: Family-owned hotel, established in 1927, on a quiet residential street on Manhattan's Upper East Side between Madison and Park Avenues
best_for: Travelers who want a residential-style base a short walk from Central Park and Madison Avenue
Guests who want a room with a wood-burning fireplace

facts.text: The Lowell is at 28 East 63rd Street on Manhattan's Upper East Side.
The hotel sits on a quiet, tree-lined residential street between Madison Avenue and Park Avenue.
Guests are steps from Madison Avenue's luxury boutiques and a 5 minute walk from Central Park.
The Lowell was established in 1927 and is one of the few remaining family-owned hotels in New York.
The hotel is privately owned by the Chartouni family.
Rooms and suites are inspired by designer Michael Smith's residential style, and features include original wood-burning fireplaces.
Many rooms and suites can be connected and feature kitchenettes.
Majorelle, the restaurant, serves French-Mediterranean cuisine with Moroccan influences.
Jacques Bar serves classic cocktails and small plates.
The Pembroke Room serves breakfast and weekend brunch.
The Club Room has its own bar and a fireplace.
Through a partnership, guests have access to Dior Spa New York, at the corner of Madison Avenue and 57th Street.

highlights.text: The building was built in the 1920s as a luxury apartment house; Dorothy Parker lived there for a spell, and F. Scott and Zelda Fitzgerald spent time there.
The Lily of the Valley Afternoon Tea, served at Majorelle, is a collaboration with Dior Maison.
The multilingual Golden Keys Concierge team can arrange experiences such as VIP entry to The Armory or a private after-hours tour of The Frick.
Michael S. Smith, who updated the guest spaces, is the designer behind the White House refresh during Obama's presidency.

considerations.text: Wood-burning fireplaces are limited to certain room categories; guests who need one guaranteed should contact the Reservations Team.
There is no spa at the hotel, but there is a small fitness center; the partner Dior Spa is at Madison Avenue and 57th Street.
Not all bathrooms have a bathtub, so guests should state their preference when booking.
